_about: 1-17 (wave 4a, round 1, on the build with R23's tap rules, G9, G1 and the stones): the corridor under the bridge, the only way
from the spawn block to the door room, is plugged by three crates (58 u) and a small one (30 u), and at its far end
single_block_plat_ent_890 (a 32 x 64 pillar stood on end, x 481 to 513) leaves a slit 31 u high (y 160 to 191) that a 36.2 u player
cannot walk: the player has to go through a portal into the door room, and no shot reaches it until the four bodies are out.
So each of them leaves by a pair of its own, and the level costs exactly its golden score, 10 portals = five pairs.
The player walks left off the block (x 128) to the floor (lands on 47) and right under it to x 263, short of crate_ent_884 (he
touches it from x 282); the camera then shows x 35 to 490. Pair 1: a shot to (60, 180) over the far left floor (tap 150,
placed 208), the dump; then a shot to (320, 200) (tap 215): the tap-time ray ends 10 u inside the first teleportable body it
meets, crate_ent_884's face (x 291), so the second portal opens ON the crate and it goes through to the dump on tick 221,
which spends the pair, and lands at x 60. Pairs 2 and 3 do the same one crate at a time, each dump a little nearer the player
so that every ray passes the ones already there (the crates' tops, y 166, are 6 u under the block's underside): (125, 180) then
(385, 200), crate_ent_885 out on 316 (lands x 125); (190, 180) then (440, 200), crate_ent_886 out on 394 (x 190). The player
walks right to x 352 while the third crate's shot flies (350 to 386): the view must show x 530 for the last shot (it needs x 303
or more) and the small crate's shot is the flattest from here. Pair 4: (240, 200) for the small crate, then (490, 176), which
is already inside it: it goes out on 474 (lands x 240). Pair 5: a shot through the slit to (530, 170) from x 352, a ray that
clears the pillar's top (11) and the bridge's underside (14) along the whole ray (its aim holds from y 155 to 190 and from x 520
to 544); while it flies (479 to 529) the player walks the emptied corridor to x 453 and takes the three crystals on its floor
(491, 504, 517); then one just ahead of him at (468, 205): he is in it as it opens (534) and drops out at (530, 172) in the door
room, 8 u from the pillar, walks right on the floor and into the door. Won on tick 594. No achievement belongs to 1-17; the
medal is 3 (the gold one: 10 portals = the level's golden score and all 3 crystals, ComputeScore in game/sim/LevelEnd.cpp;
an 11th portal or a missed crystal gives 2, no crystal 1), 9.5 s.
THE ORDER OF EACH PAIR MATTERS: the dump first, the crate's portal second. A crate that is inside a portal when its partner is
placed afterwards does NOT go in the port (a draft that shot the small crate's portal first, on 440, and its partner on 474, left
the crate in place, both portals up, for the 226 ticks the run lasted): entries are edges, like an Area2D's body_entered
(Portals.hpp), where the original's doTeleporting asks isThereAnythingInPortal every frame (listing #6): a port gap, recorded
in out/parity/program/R4/round1_1-17.md; this route goes the way that works on both.
Margins: every tap holds for 3 ticks either side of its tick with the others fixed (a tap 26 ticks after the last passes the
400 ms and 25 do not; this route keeps 29 or more, and each shot has landed 3 ticks or more before the next tap goes down);
every walk edge is good for +-6 ticks and the medal stays 3 (a stand nearer or further changes the flights, which the taps
after it wait on; the stand for the slit shot must be at x 303 or more for the view to show the tap at x 530); the camera is
still at every tap but the seventh (402: the walk ended 16 ticks before, the aim's drift 0.28 px) and the last (0.57 px, the
camera is catching up with the walk). No knight, stone or fire is in the level.
